It combines NASA NISAR radar, NASADEM elevation, and Overture building data to show water patterns, the river corridor, and nearby buildings. A 0–10 m slider explores hypothetical rise scenarios. summary:
RIVERBED project summary
RIVERBED is a web map for the Swat River near Mingora. It uses satellite radar, elevation data, and mapped buildings to show the river’s observed footprint and which buildings are nearby.
How it works
- Compares four NASA NISAR radar passes: July and August 2026, labelled higher flow, and October and November, labelled lower flow.
- Uses NASADEM elevation data to model areas that could be inundated under hypothetical river-rise scenarios from 0 to 10 metres.
- Maps building footprints from Overture Maps. The current run includes 8,440 building features.
What the map shows
People can explore radar and terrain layers, compare observation dates, view the river corridor and nearby buildings, and move a slider to see how a terrain-based scenario changes.

The current analysis classified 206 buildings inside the observed corridor and 727 within 50 metres of it. The model’s radar overlap was modest: about 0.30 for calibration and 0.34 for testing.
details:
RIVERBED is an interactive web map focused on the Swat River near Mingora, Pakistan. It combines four NISAR radar observations with NASADEM elevation data and Overture building footprints. Our Python pipeline uses Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy, SciPy, and pysheds to create water masks, map the observed river corridor, estimate height above the channel, and prepare hypothetical river-rise scenarios from 0 to 10 metres. The website uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and MapLibre GL JS, with deployment on Vercel.

Users can explore radar and terrain layers, compare observation dates, view nearby building exposure, and adjust the scenario slider. In the current run, 8,440 building features were mapped; 206 were classified inside the observed corridor and 727 within 50 metres. This combines NASA radar with local exposure information to support awareness and planning discussions.

We considered radar shadow, terrain-data errors in steep areas, limited observation dates, and gaps in building data. Radar-model agreement was modest, so the slider shows a terrain-based “what if” scenario. RIVERBED does not predict floods or their timing, establish legal river boundaries, or identify places as safe.
